text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The "Iraq file" a major issue in King Hussein's coming talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton; Jordanian officials optimistic king can persuade Washington to lift U.N. sanctions amid positive indications.
- World Bank to provide $1 billion to Jordan over five years to support structural economic reforms; the plan covers the social safety net, education, water, transport and health.
- King Hussein leaves Mayo clinic and no signs of cancer detected after routine checks.
- Crown Prince Hassan says Jordan's success in economic reforms open the door to forign investment.
- Crown Prince Hassan emphasises importance of lifting trade barriers between countries in a meeting with a senior Vietnamese officials.
- King Hussein expected to meet U.S. President Clinton on April 1.
- Amendments in the Jordan Valley Authority laws which will allow an increase in length of leasing arrangements.
- Jordan seeks to build relations with Vietnam, regent tells visting team.
